correctness.rationale: From the sixteen explicitly defined 6-point row/column blocks, the enumerated face set has exactly 808 nonempty faces and vector (16,120,320,240,96,16). The inspected standalone verifier specifies 375 Forman matched pairs and complete acyclicity on 2736 Hasse covers, leaving one 0-, one 1-, and 56 2-cells. Independent reconstruction (not just saved logs) reproduced 808 faces, 375 matched pairs, a 808-node topological sort, and signed Morse degree multiset {-2:9,0:38,+2:9} for the rook labeling. A degree-2 attachment creates RP2; the other even-degree attachments are null in pi1=Z/2 and give 55 S2 summands. The explicit 16-block point permutation also identifies the Shrikhande-neighborhood complex with the rook one. This proves the full finite homotopy assertion, not just mod-p homology.

originality.rationale: A separately published exact calculation for THE SAME rook/H(2,4) open-neighborhood complex already establishes both an acyclic Morse model with one 0-cell, one 1-cell and 56 2-cells and integral H1=Z/2. These statements logically entail RP2 wedge 55 S2: the 2-complex is the homotopy cofiber of a map from a wedge of 56 circles to a circle, classified by an integer degree vector (d1,...,d56); H1=Z/gcd(d_i)=Z/2 forces gcd=2. A self-homotopy equivalence of the domain bouquet inducing a GL(56,Z) Smith/Nielsen transformation takes this map to degrees (2,0,...,0), giving RP2 wedge 55 S2. Thus the new signed degree enumeration is a certificate for a conclusion already covered as a direct standard corollary. The Kummer blocks are exactly the rook open neighborhoods by definition; the additional Shrikhande incidence permutation does not revive independent novelty of the core homotopy claim.
